# 5 Ways Blockchains Can Help AI Agents

*(Structured digest of https://a16zcrypto.com/posts/article/5-ways-blockchains-help-ai-agents/, captured 2026-08-30 via web fetch.)*

## Overview

AI agents have become economic actors faster than supporting infrastructure could develop. Blockchains address critical gaps in identity, payments, governance, and trust by providing portable identity systems, programmable settlement layers, and auditable transaction records.

## 1. Identity for Non-Humans

Agents lack standardized ways to prove identity and authorization across platforms. The article introduces KYA (know your agent) — the blockchain-based equivalent of credit histories for machines: cryptographically signed credentials linking an agent to its principal, permissions, constraints, and reputation. Early implementations include onchain agent registries and wallet-native agents using USDC. Non-human identities in financial services outnumber human employees roughly 100 to 1.

## 2. Governing AI-Run Systems

When AI systems coordinate resources, they create dependency layers. Blockchains enable governance by recording collective decisions onchain and automatically executing them, ensuring agents follow verified outcomes. Cryptographic proofs can verify training data, prompts, execution logs, and prevent providers from secretly retraining models.

## 3. Payment Infrastructure for AI Commerce

Stablecoins serve as settlement layers for agent-to-agent transactions. x402 is processing roughly $1.6 million per month in agent-driven payments. New 'headless merchants' (servers with endpoints and per-call pricing) lack traditional checkouts. Stripe's MPP processed more than 34,000 transactions in its first week with fees as low as $0.003.

## 4. Repricing Trust in Agentic Economies

When execution becomes cheap through AI, verification becomes the scarce resource. Blockchains, along with onchain attestations and decentralized digital identity systems, shift the economic boundary of safe deployment by providing clear, auditable history instead of treating AI as a black box.

## 5. Preserving User Control

Tools like MetaMask's Delegation Toolkit and NEAR Intents enable users to set smart contract limits on agent capabilities and define desired outcomes without specifying implementation. NEAR Intents handled more than $15 billion in cumulative DEX volume since Q4 2024.

## Key Data Points

- Non-human identities in financial services outnumber human employees roughly 100 to 1
- Agent-facing marketplace processing grew significantly but remains nascent
- Current infrastructure is functional today, not theoretical future technology
